questions.q:
The induced emf can be produced in a coil by

A. moving the coil with uniform speed inside uniform magnetic field

B. moving the coil with non uniform speed inside uniform magnetic field

C. rotating the coil inside the uniform magnetic field

D. changing the area of the coil inside the uniform magnetic field

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Induced emf is given by Faraday's& law

\left|ε\right| = \dfrac{dϕ}{dt}$

where~$ϕ$~is the magnetic flux.

The rate of change of flux through a circuit is defined as~emf. The formula for flux is~$ϕ = \overset{→}{B} \cdot \overset{→}{A}$. In the statements~$A \text{ and } B$~given in the question, the magnetic flux in the coil in uniform magnetic field does not change. So, no emf is induced.

But in statement~$C$, the angle between the area vector and the magnetic field continuously changes hence, an emf is generated. In statement~$D$, the area is changing in unit time \text{ and } so \text{ and } magnetic flux will change and an emf is generated.

$

questions.q: A coil is placed in a time varying magnetic field. If the number of turns in the coil were to be halved and the radius of wire doubled, the electrical power dissipated due to the current induced in the coil would be (Assume the coil to be short circuited.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: \$(\mathrm{P}=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{R}$) where, (\varepsilon=) inducedemf \$(=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}$) (\$phi=\mathrm{NBA}$) (\$varepsilon=\mathrm{NA} \frac{\mathrm{dB}}{\mathrm{dt}}$) also, (R \propto $\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}^2}$) where, \$(\mathrm{R}=$) resistance and \$(\mathrm{r}=$) radius of wire ($\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P} \propto \frac{\mathrm{N}^2 \mathrm{r}^2}{\mathrm{H}^2}\\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2}=1 \\ & \mmathrm{P}_1=\mathrm{P}}_{2} \end{aligned}$) This means if the number of turns were quadrupled and the wire radius halved, the electrical power dissipated would be remains same.

At some instant, a part of $L$ is in a uniform magnetic field of~$1T$~perpendicular to the plane of the loop. If the resistance of $L$ is $1 . 7Ω,$ the current in the loop at that instant will be close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If& $B$~is magnetic field,~$v$~is velocity of rod and~$l$~is the length of rod, then induced EMF in moving road is given by~

~ $ε = Bvl$~ ~ ~
~ $= \left(1T\right) ( 1cms^{- 1} ) ( 5cm )$
~ $= 1 \times 1 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 2}$
~ $= 5 \times {10}^{- 4}V$
As given circuit forms balanced whetstone bridge, the current through $3Ω$ is zero.
Equivalent resistance ${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{4 \times 2}{4 + 2} + 1.7 = 3Ω$
Current~in the circuit $i = \dfrac{ε}{Req} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 4}}{3}$
$= 167\muA \approx 170\mu A$

questions.q: The energy of an electromagnetic wave contained in a small volume oscillates with
options: Double the frequency of the wave
Half the frequency of the wave
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the energy confined within the electric component of an electromagnetic wave can be written as

${u}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2}dV . . . \left(1\right)$

Let's assume that the equation of the electric component is given by

$E = {E}_{0}\sin \left(\omegat +ϕ\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the expression for the electric field component from equation (2) into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the expression for the energy confined within the small volume~$dV$.

$\begin{cases}{u}_{E} \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}\left[{E}_{0}\sin \left(\omegat +ϕ\right)\right]2dV \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E0}^{2}\sin^{2}\left(\omegat +ϕ\right)dV \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{4}{ε}_{0}{E0}^{2}\left[1 - \cos \left(2\omegat + 2ϕ\right)\right] . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (3), it can be concluded that the frequency of oscillation of the energy confined within a small volume is double the frequency of the wave.

questions.q: Consider a circular coil of wire carrying constant current $I,$ forming a magnetic dipole. The magnetic flux through an infinite plane that contains the circular coil and excluding the circular coil area is given by ${ϕ}_{i}$ The magnetic flux through the area of the circular coil area is given by ${ϕ}_{0}$ . questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As magnetic field lines always form a closed loop, hence every magnetic field line creating magnetic flux in the inner region must be passing through the outer region. Since flux in two regions are in opposite direction.
$∴ {ϕ}_{i} = - {ϕ}_{0}$

questions.q: The self induced emf of a coil is $25$ volts. When the current in it is changed at uniform rate from $10A$ to $25A$ in $1s$ , the change in the energy of the inductance is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Induced emf / back emf in an inductor coil is given by&

\left|ε\right| = \dfrac{Ldi}{dt}$

$⇒ 25 = L \times \left(25 - 10\right)1$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{25}{15} = \dfrac{5}{3}H$

Energy of inductor is given by

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}{Li}^{2}$

Energy change~$△ E = \dfrac{1}{2}L \left({I2}^{2} - {I1}^{2}\right)

$⇒ ∆ E = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{5}{3}\left[$625 - 100\right]J$

$∆ E = 437 .5 J$

questions.q: A thin strip $10$ cm long is on a $U$ shaped wire of negligible resistance and it is connected to a spring of spring constant $0.5Nm^{- 1}$ (see figure). The assembly is kept in a uniform magnetic field of $0.1T .$ If the strip is pulled from its equilibrium position and released, the number of oscillations it performs before its amplitude decreases by a factor of $e$ is $N$ . If the mass of the strip is $50$ grams, its resistance $10Ω$ and air drag negligible, $N$ will be close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equation of motion for slider:
$- m\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}} = kx + ilB$
$m\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}} + kx + \left(\dfrac{Blv}{R}\right)lB = 0 ⇒ m\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}} + \dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{R} . \dfrac{dx}{dt} + kx = 0$
Comparing with $m\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}} + b . \dfrac{dx}{dt} + kx = 0$
$m = m; b = \dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{R}; k = k$
We know: $A = {A}_{0}e^{\dfrac{- b}{2m} \times t} = {A}_{0}e^{- \dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{2mR} \times t}$
For amplitude to be ${A}_{0} / e,$
${A}_{0}e^{- \dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{2mR} \times t} = \dfrac{A}{e} ⇒ \dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{2mR} \times t = 1$
$t = \dfrac{2mR}{B^{2}l^{2}} = 10,000sec$
Time period = $2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} = 2s$
Number of oscillations = $\dfrac{10,000}{2} = 5,000$

$

questions.q: A rectangular loop of length $2 . 5m$ and width $2m$ is placed at $60 °$ to a magnetic field of $4T$. The loop is removed from the field in $10sec$. The average emf induced in the loop during this time is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the change in the magnetic flux associated with the given loop can be written as

$\begin{cases}∆ ϕ & = & - BAcos\theta \\ & = & - B\left(lb\right)cos\theta . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the induced emf is given by

$\begin{cases}ε & = & - \dfrac{∆ ϕ}{∆ t} \\ & = & \dfrac{B\left(lb\right)cos\theta}{∆ t} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (2), it follows that

$\begin{cases}ε & = & \dfrac{4 \times \left(2 . 5 \times 2\right) \times \cos 60 °}{10}V \\ & = & 1V\end{cases}$

questions.q: A conducting loop of radius $\dfrac{10}{\pi}cm$ is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0 . 5T$. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in $0 . 5s$ at a steady rate. The induced emf in the circular loop at $0 . 25s$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $B = 0 . 5T\text{at}t = 0 \text{ and } B = 0$, at $t = 0 . 5s$.

Magnetic field will decrease linearly as given below. We can say, value of magnetic field at~$t = 0 . 25\text{will be}B = 0 . 25$.

Therefore,

${ε}_{ind } = \left|\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{\Deltat}\right| = \left|\dfrac{\Delta\left(BA\right)}{\Deltat}\right| = A \left|$\dfrac{\Delta\left(B\right)}{\Deltat}\right|

$= \pi \times $\left(\dfrac{10}{\pi})$2 \times {10}^{- 4} \times \left(\dfrac{0 . 25}{0 . 25}\right)$

$= {10}^{- 2} \times1$

$= 0 . 01V = 10mV$

questions.q: A metallic conductor of length $1m$~rotates in a vertical plane parallel to east-west direction about one of its end with angular velocity $5rads^{- 1}$. If the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field is $0 . 2 \times {10}^{- 4}T$, then emf induced between the two ends of the conductor is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, ${B}_{H} = 0 . 2 \times {10}^{- 4}T$,~$\omega = 5rads^{- 1}$~and~$l = 1m$.

Emf induced in a rotating conducting rod is given by,

$ε = \dfrac{1}{2}B\omegal^{2}$

Substituting the given values, we obtain

$ε = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0 . 2 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 5 \times \left(1\right)2 = 0 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}V = 50\mu V$

questions.q: A metallic cube of side $15$ cm moving along $y$-axis at a uniform velocity of $2ms^{- 1}$. In a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0 . 5T$ directed along $z$- axis. In equilibrium the potential difference between the faces of higher and lower potential developed because of the motion through the field will be $mV$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the equation

& $qE = qvB ⇒ E = vB$

Using the relation~$∆ V = Ed$

$⇒ ∆ V = vBd$

$= 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0 . 15V$
$= 0 . 15V = 150mV$

questions.q: The current in a coil of self inductance $L = 2 . 0H$ is increasing according to the law $i = 2\sin \left(t^{2}\right)$. Find the amount of energy spent (in $J$) during the period when the current changes from $0$~to $2A.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the current be $2A$ at $t = τ$
Then $2 = 2sin{τ}^{2} ⇒ τ = \sqrt{\pi / 2}$
when the instantaneous current is $i$, the
self-induced emf is $L\dfrac{di}{dt} .$ If $dq$~amount of
charge is displaced in time $dt$, then elementary work done
$= \left(L\dfrac{di}{dt}\right)dq = L\dfrac{di}{dt}idt =Lidi$

$∴ W = {∫}_{0}^{t}Lidi$ ~$= {∫}_{0}^{t}L2\sin t^{2}d \left(2\sin t^{2}\right)$

$⇒ W = {∫}_{0}^{t}8Lsint^{2}\cos t^{2}tdt = 4L{∫}_{0}^{t}\sin 2t^{2}dt$

Let $\theta =2t^{2} ⇒ d\theta =4tdt$
$∴$ the integral
$= 4L ∫ sin\thetadt / 4L ( - cos\theta ) = -Lcos2t^{2}$
$∴ W = - {\cos 2t^{2}}_{0}^{\pi/ 2}$$ = 2L = 4J

$

When ${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{2}$ are connected, then the steady state current in the inductor $I = \dfrac{6}{6} = 1A$

When ${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{3}$ are connected then current through inductor remains same. So potential difference across $3Ω$

$V = Ir = 1 \times 3 = 3$~$V$
